A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeshArt, with matching authors, core methodology, and experiments. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary sections support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, and novelty analysis, including supplementary results in Table 6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds qualitative conditional generation, microwave generation, and CAGE geometry comparisons.

M1.justification: v2 adds an optional conditional-generation adaptation: Michelangelo or Radio features are linearly projected and prepended to the structure transformer, while the structure codebook and geometry transformer remain fixed (Section 9). The original hierarchical architecture and losses are retained.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's unconditional generation of chairs, tables, and storage furniture, v2 demonstrates generation conditioned on point clouds and sketches (Figures 6 and 10), plus microwaves (Figure 9). These additions substantially broaden input requirements and category coverage, although the added evaluations are qualitative.

E2.justification: CAGE already participates in the structure comparison in Table 2, but v2 newly compares its retrieved mesh geometry against MeshArt in Figure 11. The existing NAP and MeshGPT comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The added conditional experiments introduce learning conditional structure generation with a fixed structure codebook and geometry transformer (Section 9). Existing splits, training budgets, metrics, articulation sampling, surface-point counts, and rendering settings remain unchanged. Separate budgets for the added experiments are not specified.

E4.justification: Figure 11 adds focused visual cases highlighting CAGE's part collisions and inconsistent geometry. The structure-parameterization and conditioning ablations in Tables 4–5, and the 1,000-shape novelty analysis, are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The distribution metrics and novelty histogram retain the same statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are retained; for example, Table 3's MeshArt chair FID remains 40.8. v2 adds conditional, microwave, and CAGE qualitative results, while Figure 4 removes one table-object comparison example. The novelty distribution and illustrated examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(6), including the supplementary loss formulas, are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the claims about hierarchical articulated meshes, junction guidance, and expanded PartNet annotations. The headline 57.1% coverage and 209-point FID improvements are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 9 newly explains why retaining the structure codebook permits conditional generation without fine-tuning the geometry transformer, and discusses collision avoidance in the CAGE comparison. The existing physical-plausibility and dataset-scale limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly documents caching predicted junction faces for proximity-based retrieval, without establishing a changed underlying procedure. Section 9 specifies the conditional encoders, feature projection, and frozen components. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, annotation instructions, and project-page access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds MeshAnythingV2, EdgeRunner, MeshXL, and Meshtron; Section 9 cites Michelangelo and Radio for conditional inputs. The central positioning against static mesh generation and retrieval-based assembly remains stable. GRASS discussion is condensed, but its citation remains.

P1.justification: Related-work, evaluation-metric, and sampling passages are condensed or rephrased. The supplement gains a method overview and additional results headings. The main section organization and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with conditional-generation panels, microwave examples, and magnified CAGE failure comparisons. It also removes one Figure 4 row, redraws Figure 5, relocates tables, and reorganizes experimental pages. Renumbering the main ablation figure to Figure 7 creates a duplicate with supplementary Figure 7.

improvement.justification: The conditional-generation recipe and demonstrations, microwave examples, and focused CAGE comparison broaden supported applicability and make geometric advantages easier to assess. The gain is limited because the added evidence is qualitative and its experimental settings are incompletely specified, while existing quantitative validation is unchanged. Duplicate Figure 7 numbering introduces a small presentation regression.
